$comment: NB claim -> enforcement traceability map (the honesty guard). Each headline guarantee maps to the EXACT code that enforces it and the test that proves it. scripts/claim-map-check.mjs fails release-check if any enforced_by/proven_by reference goes dangling — so a gate cannot be deleted/renamed while its doc claim survives (the 'docs promise more than code enforces' regression). `kind` states the HONEST strength of each claim; this file doubles as the honest-scope index.

kinds.enforced: /nb:close BLOCKS (NOT_READY/CHECK_ERROR) when the guarantee is not met.
kinds.surfaced: Not a hard block by default — the firewall makes the truth VISIBLE (a labeled strength / a loud warning) so it can't be silently overclaimed; becomes a hard block under a stricter profile.
kinds.advisory: Recorded/derived state, not a runtime block over the model's behavior (e.g. model_policy is a tier string, not the actual model).
kinds.floor: Tamper-EVIDENT, not tamper-proof: holds against accidental/agentic overclaim, not a malicious user with .nb write access.

claims.claim: A pack proof_type is bound to the command it must have run — not a decorative label (an exit-0 `npm test` can't satisfy `migration-down`).
An objective proof passes only if a matching command was independently logged by the hook (a fabricated 'tests passed' with no real run is rejected).

enforced_by.contains: not observed to actually run (fabrication guard)

claims.claim: Release-/supply-critical proofs (publish-file-list, security-report-check) require a run_id from their own gate-running producer — a hand-written record is rejected.
The security red/blue gate is real cross-family: a non-Claude family claim needs a logged codex run via the courier.
The core review carries a provenance STRENGTH (cross-family machine-bound / manual / unverified) — a bare file is never silently credited as a cross-family review.
The opt-in TDD gate proves test-first: a red (failed) test run logged BEFORE a green (passed) one.
Artifacts/proofs are scoped to the current task by exact slug, not substring — another task's files can't be laundered in.
An artifact-ledger row counts only if the file it references actually exists and is task-matched (a forged row is not the artifact).

enforced_by.contains: is not itself proof the artifact exists

claims.claim: The security safety floor can never be N/A-waived — an auth/secret/payment change always has to produce its security report.
close refuses to certify 'done' from a pre-work or blocked state (idle/design/blocked).
The firewall's contract source can't be swapped via env (NB_PACKS_DIR/NB_CONTRACT_ROOT) — close fails CHECK_ERROR.
An install of a non-existent (hallucinated) package is caught by a live registry existence check.
NB's own runtime never executes JS from a string (no eval/Function/vm/shell:true) — enforced as a release gate.
A sandbox attack is authorized only when all pins pass (consent, ownership-of-a-clone, allowlist, no-destructive, no-real-payment, rate) — fail-closed.
Known secret patterns are redacted from the machine output NB writes (tool log, nb-run evidence/proofs, attack authorization).
A non-security pack N/A waiver is a human-accountable decision, not a verified proof — surfaced loudly, never a silent skip.
model_policy is a portable, recorded TIER (raise-only, gated at close) — NOT runtime control or observation of the actual model.
